ACQUISITIONS
eo This directory has been prepared to provide users of the National Law
Enforcement. Telecommunications System (NLETS) with an organized and
cross-referenced list of criminal justice agency addresses using the
Federal Bureau of Investigation's ORI's. It is the culmination of a
four year LEAA supported effort to improve interstate telecommunications
for criminal justice.
During the period from 1973-1977, the NLETS network has evolved from an
overburdened, low-speed teletype system to a high-speed, fully automated
message routing system serving law enforcement agencies in the fifty
states. Excellent service is now available to NLETS users at a reasonable
cost. ;
© The preparation and publication of this directory is a continuation of
. the overall effort to provide service to NLETS users, and will serve as
an easy to use reference listing of the addresses of local, state and
Federal criminal justice agencies in the U.S. and Canada which have
access to or are accessible through the NLETS network.
LEAA would like to express its appreciation to the Federal Bureau of
Investigation for their cooperation, and especially for their willingness
to provide the NCIC magnetic tapes of ORI addresses, without which the
publication of this document could not have taken place.
A. PURPOSE
NLETS is a nationwide message switching system created to provide
for the interstate exchange of criminal justice and criminal
justice related information. To facilitate this exchange, NLETS
utilizes the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) ORI's as addresses.
The principle purpose of this directory is to provide law enforcement
and criminal justice users with the ability to easily locate an
agency's ORI based on the name and/or location of that agency.
© B. CONTENT AND ORGANIZATION
The directory is divided into four parts. Within each subdivision,
agencies have been sequenced to provide maximum usability by the
NLETS user.
Part I - Law Enforcement Agencies
This section, subdivided by state, is sequenced alphabetically by
agency name. In addition, agencies are also listed under the city
in which they are located if the city name and the agency name
differ. These additional entries are asterisked (*) and indented. .
State agencies may be found under both their name as well as the
@ ~ location of the agency.
Federal agencies in each state may be found at the end of each
state's listing. oe
Part II - Criminal Justice Agencies
The section, also subdivided by state, is sequenced alphabetically
by location.
Part III - Federal Agencies
This section is arranged alphabetically by federal agency name.
Within each agency, the entries are sequenced alphabetically by
location.
Part IV - Canadian Agencies @
This section is arranged alphabetically by province. Within each
province, the entries are sequenced alphabetically by location.
C. ORI CHANGES
Requests for additions, deletions, or corrections of ORI's should
be coordinated through the NCIC control terminal agency within the
users' state.
